findings.summary: ASCII Corporation was a Japanese publishing company founded in 1977 that became a major force in video game and PC software. It originated as Microsoft's Japanese sales office, created the MSX computer standard, and published the Derby Stallion and RPG Maker series. After merging with MediaWorks in 2008, it became ASCII Media Works, with its entity fully dissolved by 2010.

mechanisms.title: MSX computer standard
mechanisms.explanation: ASCII co-developed with Microsoft a standardized 8-bit home computer architecture announced in 1983, which defined hardware compatibility across multiple manufacturers.

mechanisms.title: Video game publishing and series creation
mechanisms.explanation: The company published and created several video game series including Derby Stallion, RPG Maker, and AI Shogi titles, often developing software for consoles like Family Computer and Mega Drive.
